nodes.label: Experimental design and 15N application
nodes.question: How were the microplots chosen for the WW and SB crops?
nodes.answer: For WW, microplots were chosen where uniformly growing plants were present, whereas for SB, one representative plant was identified.
nodes.paragraph: Experimental design and 15N application For each crop, 6 macroplots (WW: 3 m 8 m, SB: 3 m 11 m) were defined. Within each macroplot, a mes- oplot (1.4 m 1.4 m) and a microplot ( 30 cm) were established (Supplementary Fig. S1). In the mesoplots, we applied low 15N enrichment labeling (~ 5 at%) to determine fertilizer-derived plant N uptake and to trace translocation of fertilizer N in soil. The microplots were fertilized with high 15N enrichment (~ 60 at%) and used for gas sampling. For WW, microplots were chosen where uniformly grow - ing plants were present, for SB one representative plant was identified. Meso- and microplots remained at the same spot throughout the growing seasons. Both crops were fertilized according to their N demand and yield potential, typical for these crops in the region. WW was fertilized with 21 g N m 2 (equivalent to 210 kg N ha 1) split in two fertilizer doses of 14 g N m 2 on April 8th and 7 g N m 2 on June 11th.

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What diversification strategy is widely adopted by farmers involving pulses?
nodes.answer: The inclusion of pulses into simplified rotations is the widely adopted diversification strategy.
nodes.paragraph: 2018). The inclu- sion of pulses into simplified rotations is a widely adopted diversification strategy (Hufnagel et al. 2020), as legumes can provide an array of ecological benefits (Ditzler et al. 2021). Some examples are improved N use efficiency (St. Luce et al. 2015), N credit from biological fixation (Bell et al. 2017; Taveira et al. 2020), increased water conserva- tion (Gan et al. 2017; Seymour et al. 2012), reduced N2O emissions (Lemke et al. 2007; Liu et al. 2024), improved soil health (Lal 2017), and enhanced biodiversity (Zander et al. 2016). These valuable ecosystem services encourage farmers to include pulse crops into cereal and oilseed rotations, par - ticularly in semi-arid cropping systems, where limited water availability presents significant challenges to sustainability. Canada leads global lentil and pea production, yielding 2.9 million tonnes of lentils and 4.6 million tonnes of peas in 2021, which accounts for 45% and 31% of world produc - tion (FAO 2024).

nodes.question: What was the primary objective of the study mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The primary objective was to assess the overall performance of cropping systems with different levels of diversification over an 8-year study period.
nodes.paragraph: Wheat and pulse crops are dominant crops in the semi-arid Cana- dian prairie region, where Liu et al. (2020) reported effects of various pulse crops on productivity and soil organic car - bon in pulse-wheat cropping systems, but did not address Diversifying wheat -based cropping systems with pulse crops enhances ecosystem services 17 the impact of crop diversification with pulse crops on the overall performance of cropping systems. Further diversify - ing wheat-pulse cropping systems is considered a promising strategy to enhance the sustainability of cropping systems in this semi-arid region. The objective of this study was to assess the overall performance of cropping systems with different levels of diversification during an 8-year study period using multiple indicators collectively in the semi- arid Canadian prairies.
